old: Sense disputed: taken as 'the āvāpa is to be made with a third less (in the centre than in the limbs)'. Confidence medium on the exact arithmetic.
new: tri-bhāga-ūna 'short by a third': most simply, the āvāpa placed in the limbs is the whole less the third stationed in the centre (10.5.21). The exact arithmetic is not certain.
why: reviewer (minor): The note's arithmetic does not match 10.5.21: with two thirds in the limbs and one third in the centre, the centre is half of the limbs, not 'a third less'. The simplest reading of tri-bhāga-ūna is that the āvāpa placed (in the limbs) is the total short by the third kept for the centre. The translation itself is literal and fine; medium confidence is honest.

old: The e-text's dot after yāvad joins it to the compound; yāvat is the correlative of tāvat and is split off here.
new: The e-text's dot after yāvad joins it to the compound; yāvat is the correlative of tāvat and is split off here. The typo could equally be sambādhanam (n. acc. sg. of sambādhana 'crowding') with a dropped a; the sense is the same either way.
why: reviewer (minor): The flag is right that sambādhanm is no form, but the typed 'nm' is at least as easily a dropped a in sambādhanam (n., 'crowding', also a real word) as a mistyped anusvāra. Both give the same sense and the same translation; record the alternative in the note so the flag is not treated as certain.

old: dvi-aṅga 'two-limbed': arrays combining two of the four arms, as in 10.5.31-38 taken pairwise; literal rendering kept.

old: abhihūlika is a rare word (from √hūl 'to strike, attack'); rendered 'making an assault'. The subject is the array (vyūha) understood. Reading and sense doubtful.
new: abhihūlika is a rare word (from √hūl 'to strike, attack'); rendered 'making an assault'. The subject is the array (vyūha) understood. Reading and sense doubtful. The parallel result-clause in 10.5.47 (sahiṣṇu, 'able to endure') leaves open whether vega here is the array's own charge or the enemy's shock that it meets; the e-text's reading needs checking against the printed edition.
why: reviewer (minor): abhihūlika is not a dictionary word and the draft rightly gives low confidence; but the note should also record that the parallel 10.5.47 (evam etat sahiṣṇu bhavati, the result of the opposite placement) suggests the result here may be the array's capacity to deliver or to meet a charge (vega), so 'making a swift assault' is one guess among two. Needs a person with Kangle's text and note.

old: Charging forward, riding around, riding past, withdrawing, crushing and holding, the ring, the zigzag (go-mūtrikā), the circle, the scattered attack (prakīrṇikā), turning the back, following in column, (attack) from the front, from the two sides and from behind, protection of the broken troops, pursuit of the broken troops: these are the modes of cavalry fighting.
new: Charging forward, riding around, riding past, withdrawing, crushing and holding, the ring, the zigzag (go-mūtrikā), the circle, the scattered attack (prakīrṇikā), turning the back, following in column, protection of the broken troops from the front, from the two sides and from behind, pursuit of the broken troops: these are the modes of cavalry fighting.
why: reviewer (error): The draft makes agrataḥ pārśvābhyām pṛṣṭhataḥ a separate manoeuvre by supplying 'attack', which the text does not name, so the list gets one invented item. The three adverbs stand directly before bhagna-rakṣā and are best taken with it: protection of the broken troops from the front, the sides and the rear (every other item in the list is a noun, not a bare adverb). The Hindi even writes 'आक्रमण' without brackets.
